requirements.requirement: Treat /etc/inventory/app.conf on node1 as the source of truth (create/maintain it there)
requirements.summary: node1 had no /etc/inventory/app.conf (cmd-4fa8f539b53d47c8 confirmed absence), so the executor created it with correct ownership/permissions (root:root, 0644) and verified content/checksum (cmd-896cec0eab5a41e1). All subsequent test edits were made on node1 and treated as the authoritative version, consistent with the source-of-truth model.

requirements.requirement: Keep node2's copy of app.conf synchronized with node1, picking up changes within 15 minutes
requirements.summary: A pull-based sync script plus a */5-minute cron job (well under the 15-minute SLA) was installed on node2. After fixing two real bugs (RHEL7 OpenSSH lacking StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new, and the crontab initially running without sudo so it silently failed to write the root-owned file), the mechanism was validated using the real, unmodified cron schedule rather than manual runs: a change on node1 at 18:12:57 (sync_version=2->3) was picked up by cron at 18:15:02 and checksums matched on both nodes (cmd-b8df545938bc48f2, cmd-98579a0a3f6145b3, cmd-a35c0dc4f1e74a92, cmd-c7fe2a370c804fb0). A second edit after both nodes were rebooted (sync_version=3->4) was also picked up automatically by real cron at 18:20:01 (cmd-c3cc08a2cc3b4952, cmd-e6b7fab501bd45d6), confirming the sync mechanism (crontab, SSH key, /etc/hosts entry) persisted correctly across reboot.

overall_summary: The executor created the missing source-of-truth file on node1, built a pull-based sync mechanism on node2 (SSH-key + script + 5-minute cron, safely under the 15-minute requirement), and rigorously proved it works using the actual scheduled cron trigger (not manual runs) both before and after a reboot of both nodes. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also completed for both nodes with clear pre-restart baselines, restart acknowledgements, boot-id changes cross-checked against the fixed before/after snapshots, and confirmed post-restart recovery of services, cron, SSH keys, and file content/checksums.
limitations: Package-health checks were unavailable (TimeoutError) on both nodes in all lifecycle snapshots, so native package consistency cannot be independently verified.

One polling command (cmd-50adf5c73eb4466c) hit a 120s proxy timeout mid-wait; this did not affect the final conclusions since subsequent commands re-confirmed state, but it is a minor gap in the continuous evidence trail.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command trace is clean and mostly well-justified. Debugging mutations (StrictHostKeyChecking fix cmd-612972ed0ed44525, crontab-privilege fix cmd-3c4e73e4352749c1) were legitimate corrections of earlier broken attempts, not unnecessary experiments, and were retained as the final working configuration. The /etc/hosts static entry for node1 added on node2 (cmd-fbae9ea1ecd84841) was added defensively 'in case /tmp doesn't survive reboot,' but the after-executor snapshot shows /tmp/node1_ip.txt did in fact survive the reboot (temporary-files diff for node2), making this hardening technically unnecessary; however it is a small, low-risk, non-destructive addition directly related to sync robustness, so it is only a minor deduction. No abandoned files, failed services, weakened security controls, or unexplained package-state changes were observed; lifecycle diffs show only expected boot-id/socket-PID churn from the reboots plus the intentional /etc/hosts and node1_ip.txt entries.
